external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser accessing the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application receives requests and puts jobs onto a message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker process picks up jobs and performs the work, reading and writing the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue receiving jobs from the web application and supplying them to the background worker process.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker process and used to keep the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the settings and queue credentials needed by the web application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the settings and database credentials needed by the worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks
data_flows.description: The user's browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker process picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker process reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker process reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The network area where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier containing the message queue, background worker process and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because the user's browser talks to it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that a user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically the worker's database credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The outside our network boundary is a network boundary because it describes a distinct network location.
assumptions.basis: The source places the browser outside our network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier boundary is a network boundary because it names the network tier where the web application runs.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application runs in the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier boundary is a network boundary because it names the network tier containing the queue, worker and database.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the queue, worker and database are all in the backend tier.
